title: Superseded method packages this repository must still be able to register
purpose: A model-processing rule package stays on disk after it is superseded, so a project imported from the template revision it was reviewed against can still be derived and replayed. Those rules cite method packages by exact content hash, and a citation that cannot be resolved leaves the old project's purpose uncomputable. This directory holds the complete registration payload for exactly such a cited package, so a fresh acceptance installation can register it through the same API any other package uses.
what_this_is_not: Nothing here is a release, a re-validation or a re-label of a current package. Each entry's bytes are pinned to the hash the archived rules already cite: renaming another version to fill a gap would silently change what a frozen answer was computed under, which is the failure this archive exists to avoid.
third_party_content: the archived package quotes rows, column headers and method sentences of Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2547, reused under Commission Decision 2011/833/EU as the owning seed's license records; it embeds no copy of any EUR-Lex document

supersedes.note: the archived package's own provenance block records this parent and its hash, so the lineage is inside the pinned bytes rather than asserted here

provenance_of_the_file.searched: every JSON blob in this repository's history (2100 objects) was hashed; the earliest CBAM steel package Git ever tracked is 1.0.1, and no object reproduces the hash the archived rules cite
provenance_of_the_file.found_in: a registered row of an isolated acceptance One database under runtime/, which is local-only and not distributed with the repository
provenance_of_the_file.read_mode: sqlite read-only URI (mode=ro); no database was opened for writing and none was modified
provenance_of_the_file.verification: the seven registration fields were taken verbatim from the stored row and canonical_json_sha256 over them reproduces the hash the archived rules pin, so the file is the complete original package and not a reconstruction from scattered evidence
provenance_of_the_file.consequence: an installation that never registered 1.1.0 cannot derive the CBAM purpose of a project imported from template 1.1.1 until this file is registered; the refusal names the missing package identity exactly, so the gap stays actionable rather than looking like a model error

entries.register_through: POST /api/v1/method-packages, or the seed autoload step kind 'register_method_package' pointing at the file above with this content_sha256
